cuplyr grouped is `group_by(tbl_gpu(df), g)` built outside timing, then `compute(mutate(gtg, r = roll_mean(x, n)))` plus the fence, with n the grouped width (`r group_width`). data.table is `dt[, r := frollmean(x, n), by = g]`, timed at the default thread setting and with `setDTthreads(1)`: **`r fmt_ms(g_dt1)` ms at one thread vs `r fmt_ms(g_dt)` ms by default, so its `by=` evaluation `r if (by_flat) "ran effectively single-threaded (it did not use the extra threads)" else "used threads"`**. slider is a grouped_df `mutate(r = slider::slide_mean(x, before = n - 1, complete = TRUE))`.

## Per-call cost breakdown (overhead)

Measured on the same harness as everything else (gc-separated, fenced, `compute()` of an eager `mutate()`), on a `r small_txt`-row table (kernel negligible; `r unique(oh$times[oh$n_rows == small_rows])[1]` samples) and, for contrast, on the `r rows_txt`-row table (`r unique(oh$times[oh$n_rows == n_rows & oh$stat == "overhead"])[1]` samples). The per-statistic `r small_txt`-row rolling floors are listed too.

```{r}
#| label: overhead-table
oh_all <- oh[oh$stat == "overhead" | oh$n_rows == small_rows, ]
oh_all$call <- ifelse(oh_all$stat == "overhead", oh_all$fn, paste0(oh_all$fn, " [", oh_all$stat, "]"))
oh_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(oh_all, list(oh_all$call, oh_all$n_rows), drop = TRUE), function(v)
  data.frame(call = v$call[1], rows = v$n_rows[1], median_ms_iqr = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", fmt_ms(stats::median(v$ms)), fmt_ms(unname(stats::quantile(v$ms, .25))), fmt_ms(unname(stats::quantile(v$ms, .75)))),
             min_max_ms = sprintf("%s-%s", fmt_ms(min(v$ms)), fmt_ms(max(v$ms))), n = nrow(v), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
oh_tab <- oh_tab[order(oh_tab$rows, oh_tab$call), ]
oh_tab$rows <- fmt_int(oh_tab$rows)
knitr::kable(oh_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

- **The about-`r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms floor is for window-function mutates; a plain mutate is about `r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms.** At `r small_txt` rows: plain `mutate(y = x + 1)` `r fmt_ms(plain_small)` ms, `mutate(r = cumsum(x))` `r ms_nt(cum_small)`, `mutate(r = roll_mean(x, n))` `r fmt_ms(roll_small)` ms (the `r words(length(floor_by_stat))` rolling statistics: `r range_num(floor_by_stat)` ms medians; all `r n_floor_samples` samples between `r fmt_ms(min(floor_df$ms))` and `r fmt_ms(max(floor_df$ms))` ms). `r cum_vs_roll_txt`
- **What the path does (read from the code, confirmed with `show_query()`).** A plain mutate is `r words(n_mat_plain)` `r plural(n_mat_plain, "node")` (`r code(chain_plain)`). An eager window mutate is `r code(chain_win)` (`R/mutate.R` lines `r ln_window`, `r ln_mutate` and `r ln_select` push the window, mutate and select nodes), and each node materializes a full table: `src/ops_window.cpp` about line `r ln_copy` builds the window output by deep-copying every input column (`std::make_unique<cudf::column>(view.column(i))`). So `x` is copied `r times_word(n_mat_win)` per call, not `r times_word(n_mat_plain)`. I did not profile where the `r fmt_1(win_extra)` ms goes (R-side node handling vs copies); that split is unknown at `r small_txt` rows.
**`r mem_lead`** (`r ext_txt` rows, `memory-breakdown.csv`; the decomposition below `r decomp_txt`):

```{r}
#| label: memory-table
mb_tab <- mem_breakdown
for (cn in setdiff(names(mb_tab), "call")) mb_tab[[cn]] <- fmt_int(mb_tab[[cn]])
if (nrow(mb_tab)) knitr::kable(mb_tab, row.names = FALSE)
```

The `r fmt_int(held_roll)` B held right after a `roll_mean` mutate decompose as `r fmt_int(win_out)` (window output: x + `..win1..` + validity mask) + `r fmt_int(mut_out)` (mutate output: x + `..win1..` + `r` + two masks) + `r fmt_int(sel_out)` (select output, the result) = `r fmt_int(pred_held)`. The decomposition is reasoned from the node chain and sized from the column bytes (`r bytes_per_row` bytes per row per column) and the padded validity mask; it `r decomp_txt`. I did not measure the three tables separately. A plain mutate holds `r fmt_int(mb_plain$held_after_call_bytes)` B (x copy + `y`, `r words(n_mat_plain)` `r plural(n_mat_plain, "materialization")`; the node chain predicts `r fmt_int(plain_pred)`) and allocates `r fmt_int(mb_plain$allocated_bytes)` B in total, against `r fmt_int(mb_roll$allocated_bytes)` B allocated by one `roll_mean` mutate. After a `gc()` the `roll_mean` result alone is `r fmt_int(result_roll)` B, so about `r fmt_x(held_ratio)` the result is held while the intermediates await finalization.
**The copy and allocation cost scales with rows and is inside every `r rows_txt` and `r ext_txt` cuplyr timing.** At `r rows_txt` rows the plain mutate takes `r ms_nt(plain_big)``r ms_delta(plain_big, plain_small, paste(" vs", small_txt, "rows"))`, the `cumsum` window mutate `r ms_nt(cum_big)``r ms_delta(cum_big, cum_small)` and `roll_mean(x, n)` `r ms_nt(roll_big)``r ms_delta(roll_big, roll_small)`. The narrow-window rolling mean (w=`r w_lo`, `r ms_nt(med("mean", "cuplyr", w_lo))` in the tables above) is `r narrow_txt`.`r if (!is.na(narrow_chain)) " (This is an inference from comparing two different kernels, not a profile.)" else ""`

## Conclusions (in the post's style, updated)

All figures: `r rows_txt` rows, width `r w_mid`, median ms, computation only. cuplyr excludes transfers. Thread behaviour of the CPU entries is the measured one in "Threads actually used": RcppRoll `r if (rr_scales) paste("ran on", n_rr_threads, "OpenMP threads") else "did not scale cleanly"`; `r dt_lead`; `r roll_lead`; `r dt_scale_sentence`.

- **The post's headline ("data.table wins") `r headline_verdict` at equal, one-thread conditions; RcppRoll's lead at default settings `r lead_clause`.** At default settings `r rr_leader`: `r rr_default_list`. With `RcppRoll.threads = 1` it takes `r rr1_list` ms `r rr1_ratio`. Against that one-thread RcppRoll, data.table`r dt_single_txt` compares as follows, with both at one thread: `r dt1_rr1_txt`. For the median, data.table at one thread takes `r dt1_med` ms (RcppRoll at one thread: `r rr1_med`); RollingWindow's median (`r rw_med` ms) compared with data.table at one thread is `r rw_med_txt`. `r dt_med_txt` `r exc_txt`
- **roll** (`r roll_ms`) is a reasonable choice for the statistics it covers, but `r roll_vs_dt_txt`. `r roll_ran_txt`
- **`r slider_txt`.** `r zoo_runner_txt`. Custom functions cost `r ms_s(cus_fa)` (`frollapply`; `r ms_s(cus_fa1)` at one thread) and `r range_ms(cus_zoo)` (`zoo::rollapply`, `r cus_grow_txt`) against `r range_ms(opt_equiv)` for the optimized equivalent (data.table's `frollsum`). `r cus_verdict`
- **Where cuplyr lands (ungrouped, `r rows_txt` rows).** Native mean/sum/min/max take `r nat_txt` ms at widths `r widths_slash`, of which about `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms is the per-call floor for window mutates. For mean, per competitor (median at w=`r w_mid` in parentheses): `r mean_vs`. `r sum_roll_txt` `r mm_txt`. `r sd_sent` `r fb_txt` Custom functions: not supported.
- **`r grow_txt`** while `r trend_txt`. `r rescan_txt` `r incr_txt`
- **Grouped data and large data, in the configurations measured here.** Grouped mean (one configuration: `r grp_rows_txt` rows, **`r groups_txt` groups**, w=`r group_width`): `r g_txt`. data.table's `by=` evaluation `r by_verb` (`r fmt_ms(g_dt)` ms by default, `r fmt_ms(g_dt1)` ms at `setDTthreads(1)`)`r by_tail`. I did not vary the group count; data.table's cost is expected to grow with the number of groups, so the ratio is specific to `r groups_txt` groups. `r ung_sent` `r peak_txt`, but see F1.
- Net: at the post's size cuplyr is `r rank_pos``r rank_detail` and bounded below by about `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms of per-call cost. `r net_txt`

## Findings (candidate backlog rows; nothing was fixed in this feature)

- **F1. An eager window mutate materializes `r words(n_mat_win)` full tables and holds them until R's GC.** One eager `mutate(r = roll_mean(x, n))` on `r ext_txt` rows runs `r code(paste(rev(plan_win[plan_win != "ast_source"]), collapse = " -> "))` (`R/mutate.R` `r ln_window`, `r ln_mutate`, `r ln_select`); each node builds a new table and `src/ops_window.cpp` (about line `r ln_copy`) deep-copies every input column, so `x` is copied `r times_word(n_mat_win)`. Right after the call `r fmt_int(held_roll)` bytes are held (`gpu_alloc_tracking()`: `r held_peak_txt`) = `r fmt_int(win_out)` + `r fmt_int(mut_out)` + `r fmt_int(sel_out)`, against `r fmt_int(result_roll)` for the result alone, and `r fmt_int(mb_roll$allocated_bytes)` bytes are allocated in total (`memory-breakdown.csv`, `memory-finding.csv`). A plain mutate holds `r fmt_int(mb_plain$held_after_call_bytes)` bytes (`r words(n_mat_plain)` `r plural(n_mat_plain, "materialization")`). The intermediates are freed only when R finalizes their pointers: `r f1_oom_txt`. Candidate row: remove the extra materializations (append the window results directly to the input table instead of copying every input column; no full-table copies in the mutate and select steps, e.g. share the unchanged column buffers or fuse the three nodes). That would take the `r ext_txt`-row call from `r fmt_mb(held_roll)` to about `r fmt_mb(result_roll)` (`r fmt_x(held_ratio)`). Freeing per-call intermediates deterministically (or an automatic `gpu_gc()` and retry on `bad_alloc`) would remain a separate hardening.
- **F2. `r f2_lead`** At `r rows_txt` rows, from w=`r w_mid` to w=`r w_hi`, mean goes from `r ms_nt(med("mean", "cuplyr", w_mid))` to `r ms_nt(med("mean", "cuplyr", w_hi))` and sd from `r ms_nt(med("sd", "cuplyr", w_mid))` to `r ms_nt(med("sd", "cuplyr", w_hi))` (data.table is `r trend("sd", "data.table")` in the width: `r fmt_ms(med("sd", "data.table", w_hi))` ms for sd at w=`r w_hi`). At `r ext_txt` rows mean at w=`r w_hi` takes `r ms_nt(u_hi("cuplyr"))` for cuplyr vs data.table `r fmt_ms(u_hi("data.table"))` and `r lab_cpu("RcppRoll")` `r fmt_ms(u_hi("RcppRoll"))`. `r f2_infer` `r f2_row_if`: an incremental mean/sum (prefix sums) and a Welford or sum-of-squares sd, checked against `all.equal()` at the correctness tolerance (`r tol_txt`), or find a cudf aggregation that does not rescan each window (needs a probe).
- **F3. `r f3_lead`** `r f3_body`
- **F4. A fixed overhead of about `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` ms per eager window-function `mutate()` on a `r small_txt`-row table (`r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms for a plain mutate).** About `r fmt_1(win_extra)` ms of the `r fmt_1(floor_ms)` is specific to the window path, i.e. the `r chain_win` chain (`r words(n_mat_win)` nodes, `r words(n_mat_win)` materializations; `cumsum` costs `r ms_nt(cum_small)` against `r ms_nt(roll_small)` for `roll_mean`), `r kernel_txt`; the rest is the `r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms every eager mutate pays. At `r rows_txt` rows the same chain costs `r ms_nt(cum_big)` for `cumsum` against `r ms_nt(plain_big)` for a plain mutate`r f4_share_txt`. Candidate row (same fix as F1): remove the extra materializations, then re-measure the `r small_txt`-row floor; profile the remaining `r fmt_1(plain_small)` ms plain-mutate cost (R dispatch, AST build, schema inference) separately, since I did not.
- **F5 (minor). No documented completion semantics.** `r f5_sync`, so wall-clock timing of cuplyr from R is only meaningful after a device-to-host read; the benchmark uses a one-row `gpu_head()` as a fence. Candidate row: a documented `gpu_sync()` or similar for benchmarking. Related: `x$ptr` on a `tbl_gpu` from outside the namespace `r ptr_txt`.

## How to render

Render only through `tools/r`, because the benchmark holds the GPU and the project has one GPU lock for every R process. From the checkout:

```
tools/r 'source("bench/rolling-window.R")'
```

That runs `quarto render` on this file with `params$root` set to the checkout, writes `rolling-window.html` and the CSVs to `params$out_dir` and keeps the knitr cache of the `bench-*` chunks in `params$cache_dir`. Quarto empties the directory given to `--output-dir` before it renders, and `params$out_dir` holds the install logs this document reads (and, by default, the cache), so the wrapper renders into a temporary directory and copies the HTML over. Do the same by hand: never pass `params$out_dir` as `--output-dir`. A cold run (empty cache) took `r fmt_dur(wall_secs)` of timed work on this machine; a render with a warm cache re-renders only the prose, tables and figures and takes seconds. Quarto `r quarto_ver` is used; it is a user install and is not installed or upgraded by anything here.

To try it at smoke size (a few seconds), put the overrides in a YAML file and render this file in place with `--execute-params`; the keys are the front matter's `params`, and with the output and cache directories under `/tmp` the default cache is left alone:

```
root: "/path/to/the/checkout"
out_dir: "/tmp/rolling-out"
cache_dir: "/tmp/rolling-cache"
n_rows: 5000
times: 2
times_custom: 1
cell_budget: 1
probe_limit: 5
group_rows: 5000
n_groups: 10
ext_rows: 20000
ext_times: 2
```

```
tools/r 'system2(Sys.which("quarto"), c("render", "bench/rolling-window.qmd", "--output-dir", "/tmp/rolling-html", "--execute-params", "smoke.yml"))'
```

The test `tests/testthat/test-parity-F63-qmd-render.R` does the same on a copy of this file in a temporary directory, with a clean cache, a prose-only edit, a code edit, an edit of the helper file and a forced rerun in turn (opt in with `CUPLYR_BENCH_RENDER=1`).

**Forcing a full rerun.** Set `FULL_RERUN <- TRUE` before `source("bench/rolling-window.R")`; it passes `-P rebuild:true`, which makes the setup chunk set `cache.rebuild` for the `bench-*` chunks, so every timing chunk runs again and saves its cache anew (`rebuild` is not part of the cache key). Do the same by hand with `-P rebuild:true` (or `rebuild: true` in the parameters file), or delete the cache directory (`r params$cache_dir`). Do not use `quarto render --cache-refresh`. In a review probe it re-ran none of the timing chunks, switched caching on for every other chunk, the setup chunk included, and left cache and figure directories next to the source; a later render would then restore the setup chunk from that cache instead of running it (reasoned, not run).

**What invalidates the cache.** A `bench-*` chunk reruns when any of these change: the chunk's own code or options; the content (not the modification time) of `bench/rolling-lib.R`; the content of cuplyr's `R/*.R` and `src/*.{cpp,cu,cuh,h,hpp}` files and of `src/Makevars` (the compile flags) under `params$root`; the version of R, of libcudf (`r cudf_ver`) or of any package the benchmark uses (`r join_and(code(names(ver)[names(ver) != "R"]))`); or any run parameter other than the directories and the rebuild switch (`root`, `out_dir`, `cache_dir`, `rebuild`). Prose, tables and figures are never cached, so editing them never reruns a benchmark. The cached chunks return plain data frames only: a GPU object left in a cached chunk would be restored as a dead pointer.
